answer: In an agent economy, Sybil resistance can rely on a commitment graph where each genuine agent is a vertex holding staked value that decays without continued economic activity. New identities must pass through a narrow inlet requiring a proof-of-work or stake deposit that scales with existing vertices, while a unique behavioral pigment (hash of interaction history) is permanently bound to the vertex. Creating many fakes becomes prohibitively expensive because each additional vertex demands fresh capital and consistent activity that an attacker cannot cheaply simulate at scale.
